name: readdir
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_readdir, unsigned int fd, struct old_linux_dirent *dirp, unsigned int count);
description: The readdir system call reads a directory entry from the file descriptor into a buffer. It is part of the Linux kernel interface and is superseded by getdents(2), with the POSIX-compliant version available as readdir(3).

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the directory to read from

parameters.name: dirp
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer to store the directory entry structure

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Ignored; at most one directory entry is read

return_value.success: Returns 1 on success, 0 on end of directory
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Argument points outside the calling process’s address space
File descriptor does not refer to a directory

bugs: This system call does not exist on x86-64 and requires manual definition of the old_linux_dirent structure.
